name: Grisel Syndrome
aliases: Atlantoaxial rotatory subluxation secondary to infection

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Radiological Diagnostic Criteria for Grisel Syndrome

criteria.description: Presence of torticollis with painful neck stiffness following upper respiratory tract infection or head and neck surgery
Radiological evidence of atlantoaxial subluxation or rotatory fixation on cervical spine imaging (CT or MRI)
No history of cervical trauma or congenital cervical spine abnormalities
Recent or concurrent upper respiratory tract infection, pharyngitis, or head and neck surgery

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of torticollis with painful neck stiffness plus radiological confirmation of atlantoaxial subluxation in the absence of trauma
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Early diagnosis is critical to prevent neurological complications.

pathognomonic.notes: Characteristic abnormal rotation of C1 on C2 vertebra
Head tilted and rotated with limited neck movement
searchTerms: torticollis causing neck pain and stiffness

common.symptomName: Neck pain localized to upper cervical region
History of recent upper respiratory tract infection
searchTerms: recent sore throat or cold symptoms

common.symptomName: Reduced range of cervical spine motion
Muscle spasm of cervical paraspinal muscles

occasional.notes: Difficulty swallowing due to cervical muscle spasm

searchTerms: pain localized to the back of the skull

rare.symptomName: Neurological deficits including limb weakness or paresthesia
rare.notes: Due to spinal cord compression in severe cases
searchTerms: loss of sensation or strength in arms or legs

rare.notes: Secondary to high cervical spine instability

laboratory: Elevated inflammatory markers (ESR, CRP) in presence of infection
Normal routine blood counts unless concurrent infection
imaging: CT scan showing atlantoaxial rotatory subluxation
MRI demonstrating ligamentous inflammation and spinal cord status
Dynamic cervical spine X-rays showing abnormal rotation or subluxation
other: Clinical history of recent upper respiratory tract infection or head and neck surgery

distinguishingFeatures: Often associated with trauma or congenital conditions such as Down syndrome
May lack preceding infection or inflammatory signs
Radiological evidence of fractures or dislocations without infection
Chronic joint inflammation with systemic symptoms

redFlags: Progressive neurological deficits (e.g., limb weakness, sensory loss)
Signs of spinal cord compression on imaging
references: Grisel Syndrome: A Review of the Literature and Case Report. Journal of Pediatric Orthopedics, 2018.
Atlantoaxial Rotatory Subluxation in Children: Diagnosis and Management. Pediatric Radiology, 2020.
Non-traumatic Atlantoaxial Subluxation (Grisel Syndrome): Clinical and Radiological Features. Spine Journal, 2019.
